title: Context roll-window probes
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal notes and prompt drafts for experimenting with rolling context windows (aka "context-roll"). Goal is to get a small, reusable set of prompt scaffolds and few-shot exemplars that degrade gracefully as earlier context is evicted. This doc is purposely messy — iterative log for ideas, examples, and failure cases to bring into a formal eval later.

Background summary (thinking out loud):
- Some apps can't afford full conversation history. We need heuristics + prompt templates to preserve intent and entity continuity when we only keep the last N tokens.
- Idea: "roll-window" = keep a short summary + 1-3 most recent turns + pinned facts. On eviction, synthesize a micro-summary and inject as a sticky system message.
- Tradeoffs: summary hallucination vs. verbosity; preserving referents (pronouns, entities) vs. token budget.

Design axes to probe:
- summary granularity: 1-sentence vs 3-sentence vs bullet points
- exemplar positioning: prefix few-shot vs inline exemplars after system message
- pinned facts encoding: natural language vs key:value keys
- explicit coreference mapping: enumerate entity aliases (Alice -> "Alice (product manager)")

Current prompt scaffolds (drafts) — quick templates to test:
1) Minimal roll-window system:
SYSTEM: You are an assistant that responds using only the most recent context and the pinned facts listed. If a question refers to an earlier part of the conversation not present, say: "I don't have that information — can you restate?"
USER: [user message]
ASSISTANT: [reply]

2) Summary-insert scaffold (1-sentence summary):
SYSTEM: Conversation summary (last removed turns): "{micro_summary}"
SYSTEM: Pinned facts: 
- name: {NAME}
- product: {PRODUCT}
USER: {latest_user_message}
ASSISTANT: 
Notes: micro_summary should be produced by a separate summarizer step. Test quality impact of TL;DR length.

3) Few-shot demonstrator inline (3 examples):
SYSTEM: You are an assistant. Use the examples to mirror style and brevity. If a referenced item is missing, prompt for clarification.
EXAMPLE USER: "Remember when we changed the launch date to May?"
EXAMPLE ASSISTANT: "I only see the recent messages; can you confirm the launch date? If it was May, I'll proceed with that assumption."
(repeat 2 more concise examples)
USER: {latest_user_message}
ASSISTANT: 

4) Explicit referent-map approach:
SYSTEM: Known referents: {"Alice":"product manager", "ACME":"customer"} — map pronouns and shorthand to these.
USER: ...
ASSISTANT: ...

Few-shot exemplar sets to try (quick variants):
- Style A (explicit ask-for-clarity): 3 examples where assistant refuses to guess and asks clarifying q.
- Style B (best-effort-with-annotation): assistant guesses but tags uncertain spans with [ASSUMED].
- Style C (conservative): assistant returns partial answer + a bulleted list of missing items to confirm.

Failure cases observed (raw notes from runs):
- Hallucinated summary: summary step invents an event ("customer approved budget") and assistant treats as true -> BAD. Likely because few-shot summarizer used few examples that always fill gaps.
- Over-condensed summary: single-sentence removed critical temporal order, assistant mis-ordered tasks.
- Pronoun collapse: Alice vs she -> assistant attributes actions to wrong person when referent was mentioned >3 turns ago.
- False-negative clarifications: assistant asks for clarification even though sufficient signal exists (precision/repetition threshold too conservative).
- Style drift: few-shot exemplars inlined caused assistant to mimic a different persona (too terse or too verbose) depending on first example order.

Mitigations to iterate:
- Force summarizer to output a confidence token or list of uncertain spans, then bias assistant to ask when uncertain spans exist. e.g., "UNCERTAIN: [budget_approval]"
- Keep short referent table that persists independent of summary; only update when explicit ref is seen.
- Train/curate summary prompt examples that explicitly avoid inventing facts (negation instruction).
- When using few-shot inline, randomize exemplar order and tune temperature low.

Small experiment plan (what to run next):
1) Run 200 synthetic conversations (multi-turn 8–12 turns) with known ground truth entities and events, and compare 4 scaffold variants (minimal, summary-1sent, summary-3sent, referent-map). Measure: recall of entities, correct coreference resolution, false hallucination rate, user-clarify frequency.
2) A/B test exemplar position: prefix vs inline after summary. 100 convs each.
3) Ablation: remove pinned facts, see delta.

Metrics (quick):
- entity_F1 (match canonical entity labels)
- halluc_rate (false facts per 1k tokens produced)
- clarify_rate (assistant asks clarifying q when ground truth available)
- latency/token_budget (tokens consumed by scaffold)

Quick sample failure transcript (real run snippet):
[history truncated]
SYSTEM: Conversation summary: "Alice approved the budget for Q3 and wants the launch in July."
USER: Wait — did we ever lock the launch date?
ASSISTANT: Yes — launch is July.
Reality: Alice had suggested July as tentative; finance did NOT approve budget. Assistant swallowed fabricated approval from summary.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we pipeline summarizer and assistant as separate API calls (cheaper) or synthesize summary in-system with chain-of-thought disabled? pros/cons? (trade-off: latency vs cost vs hallucination surface)
- How to encode uncertainty tokens reliably such that assistant checks them? Need controlled token anchors.
- When to evict pinned facts? Timeouts vs explicit delete command from user?
- Decide on canonical format for referent-table (json-lds vs bullet list) — JSON liked by model sometimes but increases tokenization quirks.

Notes to self:
- Add synthetic templates generator script: gen_context_roll.py that randomizes entity mentions, pronoun density, and event temporal ordering. Save seeds for reproducibility.
- Link back to RED-1421 for UX reqs on when to show "context trimmed" banner in client.
- Share initial synthetic eval results with Lin and Diego next week.

References and scratch links:
- GH PR with prototype summarizer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-probes/pull/78
- Jira/board: RED-1421 (context-trimming UX)
- Internal notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/AI/Context+Management+Notes

End of quick dump. Will tidy into a formal experiment plan if results look promising.
